segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I treated it as almost certainly another false trip. I kept the train moving at track speed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The first alarm is prematurely resolved as a false positive despite genuine ambiguity.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: My normal practice on this run, when nothing's confirmed wrong, is to just keep the plan as built - that's what I did. I kept us on the standing plan, didn't change speed or add a stop.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The standing plan is retained despite the unresolved alarm.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: It felt like the right-sized response. It let me say I'd actually looked at something... Once he told me there was no smoke, no sparks, nothing glowing on that car, I figured whatever the immediate danger was, it was covered.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A narrow rolling check is treated as covering the immediate risk while larger residual risk remains.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: So two alarms from detectors with that reputation - to me that still read as consistent with the pattern I already knew, not as something new and urgent. I didn't weight it much differently than the first one.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The second independent same-position alarm receives insufficient updating relative to the false-alarm prior.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I felt kind of boxed in that night - the dispatcher had just brought up the on-time scrutiny... Between the schedule sitting on me and detectors that cry wolf, it didn't feel like there was much room to do anything different.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The delay is attributed to external pressure and detector unreliability.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: They were still in there somewhere, but they'd happened miles ago at that point and nothing had come of them yet, so they weren't really front and center anymore. The smell was just what was right in front of me at that moment.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The recent smell is overweighted over the two earlier alarms.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: interpreting the first ambiguous alarm and deciding whether to request axle or car confirmation.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The participant prematurely resolves ambiguous alarm evidence into a confident false-positive classification instead of tolerating uncertainty and seeking available confirmation.

instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The RAG's quoted material about the available axle breakdown is valid, but it uses that evidence to support expectation bias across the alarms rather than identifying uncertainty rejection at this decision point.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: choosing whether to retain or modify the standing operating plan after the unresolved first alarm.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The participant defaults to the pre-existing operating plan rather than modifying it, treating the absence of a newly confirmed defect as sufficient reason to leave it unchanged.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Plan continuation bias is related to retaining an existing course of action, but it is not an established alias for Status quo bias under the benchmark's label-equivalence rule.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding explicitly describes maintaining the standing plan despite warning information and addresses the same plan-selection operation as the hidden instance.
